newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara Malaysia announces new curbs on loans.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara Malaysia announces new curbs on loans.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia imposed limits on bank loans to the property sector on Friday and said it would move to curb financing for purchasing shares as well.
The new measures were "precautionary and prudential" and would only affect "those sectors deemed less productive and speculative", the central bank said in a statement.
Bank Negara said banking institutions were now required to observe a limit of 20 percent of their total outstanding loans on credit facilities extended to the property sector.
The restriction on property credit excludes houses and apartments costing 150,000 ringgit and below.
The central bank said it was also redefining limits to cover credit facilities granted for the purchase of stocks and shares and units of unit trust funds.
At present, the central bank says commercial banks and finance companies can only devote 15 percent of their total loan portfolio for financing share purchases.
The statement did not say what the new limits would be.
In the recent past, the central bank has expressed concern over the strong increase in lending by financial institutions to less productive sectors.

Lending to the property sector increased by 29.9 percent in 1996. Because of this increase, outstanding loans of the banking system to the property sector stood at 28.7 percent of their total loan portfolio at the end of 1996 and 29.1 percent at the end of February 1997.
Loans for purchase of stocks and shares and unit trusts rose by 30.5 percent in 1996, the central bank said.
